clauses.text_display: You may be eligible for Carer’s Allowance if you, the person you care for and the type of care you provide meets certain criteria.
clauses.text_spoken: You may be eligible for Carer’s Allowance if you, the person you care for and the type of care you provide meets certain criteria.

clauses.text_display: Personal Independence Payment - daily living component
clauses.text_spoken: Personal Independence Payment - daily living component

clauses.text_display: Disability Living Allowance - the middle or highest care rate
clauses.text_spoken: Disability Living Allowance - the middle or highest care rate

clauses.text_display: Scottish Adult Disability Living Allowance - the middle or highest care rate
clauses.text_spoken: Scottish Adult Disability Living Allowance - the middle or highest care rate

clauses.text_display: The person you care for must already get one of these benefits: Attendance Allowance
clauses.text_spoken: The person you care for must already get one of these benefits: Attendance Allowance

clauses.text_display: The person you care for must already get one of these benefits: Pension Age Disability Payment
clauses.text_spoken: The person you care for must already get one of these benefits: Pension Age Disability Payment

clauses.text_display: Constant Attendance Allowance at or above the normal maximum rate with an Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefit
clauses.text_spoken: Constant Attendance Allowance at or above the normal maximum rate with an Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefit

clauses.text_display: Constant Attendance Allowance at the basic (full day) rate with a War Disablement Pension
clauses.text_spoken: Constant Attendance Allowance at the basic (full day) rate with a War Disablement Pension

clauses.text_display: The person you care for must already get one of these benefits: Armed Forces Independence Payment
clauses.text_spoken: The person you care for must already get one of these benefits: Armed Forces Independence Payment

clauses.text_display: Child Disability Payment - the middle or highest care rate
clauses.text_spoken: Child Disability Payment - the middle or highest care rate

clauses.text_display: Adult Disability Payment - daily living component at the standard or enhanced rate
clauses.text_spoken: Adult Disability Payment - daily living component at the standard or enhanced rate

clauses.section_title: If you care for the person with others
clauses.text_display: You cannot get Carer’s Allowance if you share the care of someone and the other carer is already claiming: Carer’s Allowance for that person
clauses.text_spoken: You cannot get Carer’s Allowance if you share the care of someone and the other carer is already claiming: Carer’s Allowance for that person

clauses.section_title: If you care for the person with others
clauses.text_display: Carer Support Payment for that person the extra amount of Universal Credit for caring for someone who gets a disability-related benefit for that person
clauses.text_spoken: Carer Support Payment for that person the extra amount of Universal Credit for caring for someone who gets a disability-related benefit for that person

clauses.section_title: If you care for the person with others
clauses.text_display: If you want to get Carer’s Allowance, speak to the other carer about changing their benefits.
clauses.text_spoken: If you want to get Carer’s Allowance, speak to the other carer about changing their benefits.

clauses.section_title: If you care for the person with others
clauses.text_display: If the other carer does not want to do that, you can still apply for Carer’s Allowance. The Department for Work and Pensions ( DWP ) will decide who should receive the benefit.
clauses.text_spoken: If the other carer does not want to do that, you can still apply for Carer’s Allowance. The Department for Work and Pensions ( DWP ) will decide who should receive the benefit.

clauses.section_title: The type of care you provide
clauses.text_display: You need to spend at least 35 hours a week caring for someone. This can include: helping with washing and cooking
clauses.text_spoken: You need to spend at least thirty-five hours a week caring for someone. This can include: helping with washing and cooking

clauses.section_title: The type of care you provide
clauses.text_display: taking the person you care for to a doctor’s appointment
clauses.text_spoken: taking the person you care for to a doctor’s appointment

clauses.section_title: The type of care you provide
clauses.text_display: helping with household tasks, like managing bills and shopping
clauses.text_spoken: helping with household tasks, like managing bills and shopping

clauses.text_display: All of the following must apply: you’re 16 or over
clauses.text_spoken: All of the following must apply: you’re sixteen or over

clauses.text_display: you spend at least 35 hours a week caring for someone
clauses.text_spoken: you spend at least thirty-five hours a week caring for someone

clauses.text_display: you’ve been in England, Scotland or Wales for at least 2 of the last 3 years (this does not apply if you’re a refugee or have humanitarian protection status)
clauses.text_spoken: you’ve been in England, Scotland or Wales for at least two of the last three years (this does not apply if you’re a refugee or have humanitarian protection status)

clauses.text_display: you normally live in England or Wales, or you live abroad as a member of the armed forces (you might still be eligible if you’re moving to or already living in an EEA country or Switzerland )
clauses.text_spoken: you normally live in England or Wales, or you live abroad as a member of the armed forces (you might still be eligible if you’re moving to or already living in an EEA country or Switzerland )

clauses.text_display: All of the following must apply: you’re not in full-time education
clauses.text_spoken: All of the following must apply: you’re not in full-time education

clauses.text_display: you’re not studying for 21 hours a week or more
clauses.text_spoken: you’re not studying for twenty-one hours a week or more

clauses.text_display: you’re not subject to immigration control
clauses.text_spoken: you’re not subject to immigration control

clauses.text_display: your earnings are £204 or less a week after tax, National Insurance and expenses
clauses.text_spoken: your earnings are £two hundred four or less a week after tax, National Insurance and expenses

clauses.text_display: If you live in Scotland, you need to apply for Carer Support Payment instead of Carer’s Allowance.
clauses.text_spoken: If you live in Scotland, you need to apply for Carer Support Payment instead of Carer’s Allowance.

clauses.text_display: If you’re from the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein, you and your family usually also need settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme to get Carer’s Allowance. The deadline to apply to the scheme was 30 June 2021 for most people, but you might still be able to apply. Check if you can still apply to the EU Settlement Scheme .
clauses.text_spoken: If you’re from the EU, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein, you and your family usually also need settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme to get Carer’s Allowance. The deadline to apply to the scheme was thirty June twenty twenty-one for most people, but you might still be able to apply. Check if you can still apply to the EU Settlement Scheme .

clauses.text_display: Your earnings are any income from employment and self-employment after tax, National Insurance and expenses.
clauses.text_spoken: Your earnings are any income from employment and self-employment after tax, National Insurance and expenses.

clauses.text_display: Expenses can include: 50% of your pension contributions
clauses.text_spoken: Expenses can include: fifty percent of your pension contributions

clauses.text_display: equipment you need to do your job, for example specialist clothing
clauses.text_spoken: equipment you need to do your job, for example specialist clothing

clauses.text_display: travel costs between different workplaces that are not paid for by your employer, for example fuel or train fares
clauses.text_spoken: travel costs between different workplaces that are not paid for by your employer, for example fuel or train fares

clauses.text_display: business costs if you’re self-employed, for example a computer you only use for work
clauses.text_spoken: business costs if you’re self-employed, for example a computer you only use for work

clauses.text_display: If you pay a carer to look after the disabled person or your children while you work, you can treat care costs that are less than or equal to 50% of your earnings as an expense. The carer must not be your spouse, partner, parent, child or sibling.
clauses.text_spoken: If you pay a carer to look after the disabled person or your children while you work, you can treat care costs that are less than or equal to fifty percent of your earnings as an expense. The carer must not be your spouse, partner, parent, child or sibling.

clauses.text_display: Example You earn £100 a week (after tax, National Insurance and other expenses) and spend £60 a week on care while you work. You can treat £50 of this as an expense.
clauses.text_spoken: Example You earn £one hundred a week (after tax, National Insurance and other expenses) and spend £sixty a week on care while you work. You can treat £fifty of this as an expense.

clauses.text_display: Payments that do not count as earnings include:
clauses.text_spoken: Payments that do not count as earnings include:

clauses.text_display: money received from an occupational or private pension
clauses.text_spoken: money received from an occupational or private pension

clauses.text_display: contributions towards your living or accommodation costs from someone you live with (they cannot be a tenant or boarder)
clauses.text_spoken: contributions towards your living or accommodation costs from someone you live with (they cannot be a tenant or boarder)

clauses.text_display: the first £20 a week and 50% of the rest of any income you make from someone boarding in your home
clauses.text_spoken: the first £twenty a week and fifty percent of the rest of any income you make from someone boarding in your home

clauses.text_display: a loan or advance payment from your employer
clauses.text_spoken: a loan or advance payment from your employer

clauses.text_display: You cannot get the full amount of both Carer’s Allowance and your State Pension at the same time.
clauses.text_spoken: You cannot get the full amount of both Carer’s Allowance and your State Pension at the same time.

clauses.text_display: If your pension is £86.45 a week or more, you will not get a Carer’s Allowance payment.
clauses.text_spoken: If your pension is £eighty-six point four five a week or more, you will not get a Carer’s Allowance payment.

clauses.text_display: If your pension is less than £86.45 a week, you’ll get a Carer’s Allowance payment to make up the difference.
clauses.text_spoken: If your pension is less than £eighty-six point four five a week, you’ll get a Carer’s Allowance payment to make up the difference.

clauses.text_display: If your State Pension is more than £86.45 a week, you will not get a Carer’s Allowance payment but your Pension Credit payments will increase instead.
clauses.text_spoken: If your State Pension is more than £eighty-six point four five a week, you will not get a Carer’s Allowance payment but your Pension Credit payments will increase instead.

clauses.text_display: You might be eligible for Carer’s Credit if you’re not eligible for Carer’s Allowance.
clauses.text_spoken: You might be eligible for Carer’s Credit if you’re not eligible for Carer’s Allowance.
